original_functions.quote:
Sec. 2 . Functions of the Committee, (a.)  The Committee shall, to the 
extent permitted by law and as provided by Section 1(c)(2)  of the Act, 
develop relevant information for and respond to the requests of the 
Mediator. The Mediator shall be appointed by the Director of the Federal 
Mediation and Conciliation Service pursuant to Section 1(a)  of the Act, 
and shall facilitate the compilation and development of information 
concerning negotiations under the Act.

termination_notice_records.quote:
Sec. 4. The Committee shall terminate upon the completion of the 
Mediator’s duties, as determined in accordance with the provisions of 
Section 1(a)  of the Act. The Mediator shall advise the Chairman when 
his duties have ceased. Any records which may have been maintained by 
the Committee shall be transferred to the Secretary of the Interior.

amendment.quote:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act to provide for final settlement of the conflicting rights and interests 
of the Hopi and Navajo Tribes concerning lands within the reservation 
established by the Executive order of December 16, 1882, and lands 
within the reservation created by the Act of June 14, 1934, and for 
other purposes (Public Law 93— 531, approved December 22, 1974, 
hereinafter referred to as the A ct), and as President of the United States 
of America, Section 2(a)  of Executive Order No. 11829 of January 6, 
1975, is hereby amended to read as follows:
“ Sec. 2. Functions of the Committee, (a.)  The Committee shall, to 
the extent permitted by law, and as provided by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act, develop relevant information for and respond to the requests of the 
Mediator who shall be appointed by the Director of the Federal Media­
tion and Conciliation Service pursuant to Section 1(a)  of the Act, in 
order to facilitate the expeditious and orderly compilation and develop­
ment of factual information relevant to the negotiation process estab­
lished by the Act.”

amendment_signature.quote:
T h e W h ite H o u s e,
April 17,1975.

revocation.quote:
Sec. l l .  Executive Order No. 11829, as amended, establishing the Hopi-Navajo  
Land Settlement Interagency Committee, is revoked.

independent_findings: The complete original can be represented by seven substantive units: section 1 establishment/membership; section 2(a) information/mediator functions; section 2(b) meetings/liaison; section 3 support; and the three separate sentences of section 4 (conditional termination, notice, records transfer). No sentence of section 4 may be dropped.

Section 4 ties Committee termination to completion of the Mediator duties, determined in accordance with section 1(a) of Public Law 93-531. Notice to the Chairman is separately required. Neither the negotiating time limit cross-reference nor any assumed deadline supplies the actual completion determination. The full cited statute and the historical completion/notice record were not found in the inspected local source records/text search.

EO11853 substitutes all of original section 2(a); its full text bears April 17, 1975 and no deferred effective clause. That is an actual partial amendment, not a whole-order termination. Its revision removes the standalone original sentence directing the Mediator to facilitate compilation and reframes Committee duties to facilitate factual information for negotiation. Section 4 is not amended.

The original section 2(a) wording is superseded by the amendment if still in force then. If the Committee own-terms termination had occurred earlier, that earlier event would govern earliest cessation. No exact first-end can be filled simply from the amendment date without addressing that actual occurrence gap.

EO12379 section 11 expressly revokes EO11829 as amended. Its complete text has no delayed effective date or savings for this target. August 17, 1982 is supported as formal revocation, not automatically earliest termination of the Committee or completion of record transfer.

Section 4 separately requires any Committee records to be transferred to the Secretary of the Interior. This is concrete wind-down language, not a hypothetical residual. The transfer occurrence, completion and subsequent independent custody obligations are distinct from the existence of the Committee.

The original and amendment are complete, unambiguous official extracts with matching issue-PDF fixity rows; no page image was inspected and no retained PDF is claimed. Missing images alone are not treated as a legal blocker. Root retention-job activity is not evidence of new local bytes.
